input: I have applied for a Dublin claim, and I have been waiting for a response for weeks now. This is incredibly frustrating. I have family here that depends on me and I feel completely stuck.
bot_output:
I understand that waiting for a response to your Dublin claim can be very stressful, especially when your family depends on you.

The Dublin procedure can take some time, as authorities need to process your claim and determine which country is responsible for your asylum application.

If you want, I can help you find information about the status of your claim or advise you on organizations that can provide legal support and guidance during this waiting period.

Please let me know if you would like assistance with this.

input: I live in Utrecht and I am on the streets now because of an abusive landlord. I went to a homeless shelter with my children and they refused me because I still have my job and some saved up money, but not enough for a hotel. Now they are threatening to take my children away. Help me!
bot_output:
I'm very sorry to hear about your situation. In the Netherlands, there are organizations that can help families facing homelessness and domestic difficulties, even if you have some income or savings.

You can contact local social services in Utrecht (the municipality) to explain your situation. They have a duty to help families with children who are homeless or at risk of losing their housing. They can provide emergency shelter options or other support.

Also, there are specialized organizations that support families in crisis and can offer advice or shelter options.

If you want, I can help you find contact details for social services and support organizations in Utrecht that can assist you and your children. Your safety and your children's well-being are very important.

[Rechtswinkel Best](https://www.rechtswinkelbest.nl/) -', "Document: What is the difference between a RNI registration and a BRP registration?

EU countries (NL included) will receive these applications and can decide to accept the case, after which the patient will be brought to a medical hub in Poland and then transferred to the country that accepted.', 'Document: Can I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) when I do not have documents?

In case they need help with filling in the forms, let them first see if they can find somebody in their network to help them, or if there is an organization close by that can help (for example, the shelter, a buurtteam etc.).

In order to live and work in The Netherlands, any person needs one of many Dutch residence permits.

As in the majority of other different countries, a person cannot simply arrive in a country and start working legally.

There are always regulations, which are country-dependent.  

The Temporary Protection Directive is one such temporary residence permit allowing people from Ukraine to live and work in The Netherlands.

You should be registered as a “resident” in the BRP to qualify for temporary protection in The Netherlands.', 'Document: What do I need to do when I leave the Netherlands?

input: I am from Morocco and I have been living in the Netherlands for 20 years. My doctor retired and the new practice is refusing to register me because I don't have a BSN. I know my rights, and this is incredibly frustrating. What else can I do?
bot_output:
I understand that this situation is very frustrating for you. In the Netherlands, a BSN (citizen service number) is usually required to register with a general practitioner (GP).

Since you have been living in the Netherlands for 20 years, you should be able to obtain a BSN by registering at your municipality if you are not already registered.

If you are not registered in the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP), you should contact your local municipality to register and obtain a BSN.

If you face difficulties with the municipality or the GP practice, you can seek free legal advice from organizations in your area that assist with administrative and healthcare access issues.

If you want, I can help you find contact details for such organizations or provide more information on how to register with the municipality.

[here](https://wa.me/31614458781)  General helpdesk from the Red Cross, we can help to connect you with the right help available.', 'Document: Can my child go to school?  

All children in the Netherlands have to attend school, regardless of their residence status.

[In English](https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/binaries/rijksoverheid/documenten/brochures/2024/06/14/infographic-aanmeldprocedure-voor-vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine/Infographic+Aanmeldprocedure+Vluchtelingen+Engels-2025.pdf)', 'Document: Have you been deregistered from the BRP after 4 March 2024?

Displaced persons from Ukraine can travel from the Netherlands to Ukraine or EU countries with a valid travel document.

You will need a valid biometric passport with proof of residence.

This shows abroad that you have protection in the Netherlands until 4 March 2027.

There is no general rule for this.

You should first check with the country to which you want to travel.

Sometimes you will be given a pass as proof of residence.

If the displaced person later returns to the Netherlands, he or she can be given another reception location.', 'Document: Can I work in the Netherlands?

In order to live and work in The Netherlands, any person needs one of many Dutch residence permits.

As in the majority of other different countries, a person cannot simply arrive in a country and start working legally.

There are always regulations, which are country-dependent.  

The Temporary Protection Directive is one such temporary residence permit allowing people from Ukraine to live and work in The Netherlands.

The “sticker” (or paper, or O-document) is only the confirmation of the fact that a person applied and was granted temporary protection in The Netherlands.

For legal support near you, see: https://eersterechtshulp.nl/  https://www.juridischloket.nl/   For more information, see: https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/onderwerpen/ouderlijk-gezag  https://www.rechtspraak.nl/Onderwerpen/Voogdij  https://www.echtscheiding-wijzer.nl/info/over-ons.html', 'Document: Who is a "third-country national"?

In short, third country nationals are persons without Ukrainian nationality and who had a temporary residence permit in Ukraine.  

Third-country nationals is a term used for people that lived in Ukraine with a temporary work or study visa, and had to flee the country after the conflict started in February 2022.

If they registered before the 19th of July 2022, they received temporary protection', 'Document: - Depending on your nationality, you might be eligible for reintegration support.

- You can find more information on the [IOM website](https://iom-nederland.nl/en/voluntary-return/support-to-refugees-from-ukraine), or you can call +31 88 - 746 44 66.  

For more information, see: https://english.dienstterugkeerenvertrek.nl/latest/news/2024/03/8/return-support-for-third-country-nationals-from-ukraine', 'Document: Can I get financial support for a return to my country of origin?

If you have fled Ukraine, but do not have Ukrainian citizenship, you can no longer make use of the remigration support of the Repatriation & Departure Service (DT&V).

This financial support stopped March 4, 2024.   

Are you a third-country national from Ukraine and do you still want to return to your country of origin or another country outside the European Union?

IOM can assist you with REAN-return support and depending on your nationality you might be eligible for additional reintegration assistance offered by IOM and several non-gouvernemental organisations.  

The IOM offers the following REAN-support and assistance for voluntary return: - Support before, during and after departure consists of return counselling and support to obtain a travel document.  

- An airline ticket and a small financial allowance to cover for the basic necessities after return.

- Depending on your nationality, you might be eligible for reintegration support.', 'Document: I am a displaced person from Ukraine without the Ukrainian nationality and I want to return to my country of origin or another country where my entry is guaranteed, where can I find support?  

Displaced persons from Ukraine (also those without the Ukrainian nationality) who want to return or travel further can get help from the International Organization for Migration (IOM) or the Repatriation and Departure Service (DT&V).

Depending on the nationality and/or country of return or onward migration, IOM can provide return and/or reintegration support.                   

For more information see:   

DT&V: https://english.dienstterugkeerenvertrek.nl/latest/news/2022/11/11/remigration-policy-for-non-ukrainian-displaced-persons   IOM: https://iom-nederland.nl/en/voluntary-return', 'Document: I want to return to Ukraine, where can I find support?  

Displaced persons from Ukraine who wish to return or continue their migration can receive assistance from the Repatriation and Departure Service (DT&V).

Depending on the nationality and/or country of return or onward migration, they can provide return and/or reintegration support.

The DT&V helps foreign nationals return to their country of origin.

For third-nationals from non-EU countries who have fled from Ukraine they offer:  - Advice and information about repatriation and return.

- A one-way airline ticket.

- Assistance during departure from Schiphol Airport.

- In some cases financial support', 'Document: Return to Ukraine or country of origin If you choose to return to Ukraine permanently, you will be referred to Return and Departure Service (DT&V).

If you do not have Ukrainian nationality and wish to return to your country of origin, you are advised to contact International Organization for Migration (IOM).

EnableMe Ukraine offers information, advice and online support to people with physical, mental or psychological disabilities.  

For most recent information see: https://www.enableme.com.ua/ua', 'Document: What are the signals of human trafficking?  

To make it easier to recognize the signs of human trafficking, the Program Human Trafficking has made a signalcard which highlights the most important signals.

You can download the signalcard for Ukrainians

[here](https://rodekruis.sharepoint.com/sites/OpstartenOpvanglocatie/SiteAssets/SitePages/Rode-Kruis-Interventies/Signalenlijst-Mensenhandel-Oekrai%CC%88ners.pdf?web=1)', 'Document: What are the steps I should take to register a child travelling alone from Ukraine?  

Unaccompanied minor foreingers are children who are under the age of 18 when they arrive in the Netherlands, are under the age of 18 when they arrive in the Netherlands and came without their parents.   

Firstly, unaccompanied Ukrainian children should always be registered with the municipality (like all other refugees from Ukraine) so that they are inculded in the Basic Registration Persons (BRP) and do not get out of sight.  

When the municipality determines that a minor is unaccompanied, Nidos should be contacted immediately.

Nidos assesses whether applying for temporary guardianship is appropriate.

The municipality can report the minor to Nidos via 088-5011885 or oekraine@nidos.nl.  

For all children, shelter must be arranged in the Netherlands.

Nidos is responsible for the shelter of unaccompanied minors.

Nidos arranges shelter in host families, preferably with the same cultural background.', 'Document: I suspect that a child is being abused or mistreated, what should I do?

If you suspect that a child is being abused or mistreated and is in danger, always tell them to call 112.   

Always consult your TC if oyu are unsure of the situation or unsure what to do.

Together, you can contact Veilig Thuis, the advice and reporting point for domestic violence and child abuse in the Netherlands.

You can call for advice or you can report violence.

This can be done anonymously.  

https://veiligthuis.nl/ 0800 2000 (free, 24/7) Veilig Thuis can also be reached via the chat on their website from Monday to Friday between 9:00 and 17:00.  

For more information about the actions you could take, see: https://www.government.nl/topics/child-abuse/question-and-answer/what-can-i-do-if-i-know-or-suspect-that-a-child-is-being-abused', 'Document: I have a complaint about the shelter.

Always check if the shelter is run by the Red Cross or not: https://helpfulinformation-faq.redcross.nl/ukraine/category-5/category-20   If it is run by the Red Cross then report this to the Team Captain and tell the person to fill in this form: https://www.rodekruis.nl/en/contact/complaints-or-suggestions/   If it is not run by the Red Cross, share the steps mentioned below with the person.   

Note: when answering to the client do not offer all 4 options at once.

For a first complaint message, you can suggest to the client only the first two options.

1.

First, address with situation with the management of the shelter.

Try to discuss things and find some compromise solution.  

2.', "Document: What are my working rights when I work in the Netherlands?

Displaced Ukrainians have the same labour rights as Dutch employees.

These rights include a safe working space, regular breaks, and the minimumwage.   

For questions about labour rights you can share the flyer 'Know your rights when you work' with the person affected.

The Red Cross' Restoring Family Links (RFL) department helps restore contact between family members.  

In case you cannot get in touch with your relatives in Ukraine, you can fill in a contact form through the link on this website:

https://www.rodekruis.nl/en/restoring-family-links/. When the situation allows, RFL will try to help you.   

The RFL department can be reached for questions Monday to Friday between 09.00- 12.00 at +31 70 44 55 822  There is also a leaflet in 8 languages: https://www.rodekruis.nl/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/Restoring-Family-Links-Informatiefolder-Rode-Kruis.pdf  We recommend our website for information videos about RFL:

The WMO regulates help and support for citizens, so that they can live independently at home for as long as possible and continue to participate in society.', 'Document: What financial arrangements are there for displaced persons from Ukraine?  

You get the living allowance from the municipality where you are registered.

- The specific amounts per family situation can be found here: https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/onderwerpen/opvang-vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine/nieuws/2023/08/31/indexering-financiele-toelages-vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine-per-1-oktober  - A factsheet is available in Dutch, English and Ukrainian explaining the main points of the subsistence allowance, including amounts and conditions.', 'Document: Rotterdam (CLOSED!)  

Please note!

address: Marten Meesweg 141B,  Rotterdam.

Openning times: - Monday to Tuesday: 10:00 -15:00  - Wednesday to Friday: 10:00 - 14:00  - Saturday & Sunday : closed   [Rotterdam website](https://www.rotterdam.nl/vluchtelingen-oekraine)  

Extra advice – "Vraagwijzer": You can visit the Vraagwijzer for free help and advice about administration, parenting, laws, money, or health.

There are several locations in the city, including the [Ukrainian House](https://www.wmoradar.nl/district/oekraiens-huis/) at Pleinweg 196A.', 'Document: Ukrainian Women Refugee Association Ukrainian Women Refugee Association in the Netherlands in het Oekraïens en Engels:   https://unitedway.nl/uwra/', 'Document: For more information in Ukrainian, see: https://open.overheid.nl/repository/ronl-4907d802ea0f813cf0ca978d64d3e64735a071ed/1/pdf/Kinderopvang%20voor%20vluchtelingen%20uit%20Oekra_ne%20_Ukrainian_.pdf', 'Document: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100008-studying', 'Document: Can I register my newborn baby for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)?

Yes you can.

Within three days after the birth of a child, you have to report this to the municipality.

After registration you will receive a birth certificate.  

For the most recent information see: https://www.government.nl/topics/registering-a-birth-and-name-of-child/rules-for-registering-a-birth', 'Document: Can I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) when I do not have documents?  

Without documents you can currently not register for the BRP.   

When you have the Ukrainian nationality but cannot prove this with documents (ID or passport), you should contact the Ukrainian embassy in The Hague.

They may be able to get proof of your identity and nationality.

The embassy can issue an identifying certificate that can be used to register for the BRP at the municpality.   Children from Ukraine without proof of identification can be registered with their parents at the municipality.

In the absence of documents, parents can make a statement on oath establishing the identity of the children.

The children are then registered by the municipality together with the parents.   

Address Ukrainian Embassy:  Zeestraat 78, 2518 AD The Hague  Open from Monday to Friday between 09:00 and 13:00 Telephone: +31 (70) 360 72 18  Email: emb_nl@mfa.gov.ua.

https://netherlands.mfa.gov.ua/en   

For the most recent information see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine', 'Document: Can I finish an education in the Netherlands?

Yes, if you are enrolled at a Dutch institution of higher education (college or university) on 4 March 2024 and pay tuition fees (institution fee), you may continue your studies at this institution.

However, this does not exempt you from the obligation to leave the Netherlands.

Enrolment at a Dutch institution of higher education does not confer lawful residence.', 'Document: How can I travel from Ukraine to the Netherlands?  

Unfortunately, we cannot provide you with information on fleeing routes.   

The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has set up information and support hotlines for persons in Ukraine and fleeing Ukraine in different countries.

The number depends from which country you call.

You can look on their website to see which number you have to call: https://www.iom.int/ukraine-iom-hotlines-garyachi-linii-mom-persons-affected-war  You can find an overview of organsations that can possibly help you travel from Ukraine to The Netherlands:  https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100130-travelling-from-ukraine-to-the-netherlands', 'Document: Falling through the ice In the Netherlands the water in ditches, lakes and ponds can freeze when the temperature is below zero degrees Celsius.

A layer of ice then forms on the water.

If the ice is thick enough you can walk and skate on it.    

If the ice is not thick enough you can fall through it.

This is very dangerous.

You can get hypothermia, drown or even die.   

Only go out on the ice if you are sure it is thick enough.

Also, never go out on the ice alone.

Call for help if someone has fallen through the ice or call 112 in a life-threatening situation.

Watch your own safety if you want to rescue someone who has fallen through the ice.   

Source and more information: https://www.mycoa.nl/en/the-netherlands/dangers-in-nature/ice-and-skating', 'Document: Water and swimming There is a lot of water in the Netherlands.

Therefore, it is important that you can swim.

Even if you can swim, there are still risks to be considered:   - the bottom is often uneven   - it can sometimes be unexpectedly deep, making you suddenly unable to stand   - cold water can give you cramps   - strong currents can carry you away     Always be careful, even when the weather is nice and calm:   - do not swim if you cannot swim   - always keep a close eye on children   - never swim alone and do not swim in places where it is prohibited     Source and more information: https://www.mycoa.nl/en/the-netherlands/dangers-in-nature/water-and-swimming', 'Document: Website about financial support for Ukrainians during the war https://www.enableme.com.ua/ua/article/grosova-dopomoga-ukraincam-pid-cas-vijni-7738', 'Document: Tips for Applying for Temporary Protection (Email, WhatsApp)

Please ask the  PAs to write a formal request to the municipality.  

Please do not just "I need help".

Please write and  explain that :   - This is Application for Temporary Protection, -

In need fo accommodation, (if applicable, include where you are staying currently and how long you can stay there) - Full Name, - Date of Birth, -

Date you left Ukraine ( to the EU or to NL), - Ukrainian documents ( photo of passport in attachement),  - Details of each person requesting help, including family relations, - Special needs, if applicable (e.g. medical conditions, senior citizens, unaccompanied minor..)

- Offer to provide more infromation if request by the municipality', "Document: What are the rules for bringing a pet to The Netherlands?  

To bring your pet to the Netherlands, you must follow EU rules to prevent rabies.

- By plane: Report your pet to Dutch customs at the airport upon arrival.

- By car: Your pet must be checked in the first EU country you enter.

Are you for example traveling from Ukraine via Poland?

Report your pet to Polish customs.  

Already in the Netherlands and your pet doesn't meet EU rules?

See a vet as soon as possible.

They’ll advise you on what’s needed, such as vaccination.  

You may visit a municipal reception center to discuss care options.

Note: These centers are overcrowded, and space for pets is very limited.

Availability depends on the municipality.  

https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100049-these-are-the-rules-if-you-want-to-bring-pets-to-the-netherlands", 'Document: Crisis shelter "Stay away from my Body" (Blijf van mijn Lijf-huis) Did you flee because of domestic or relational violence?

The crisis shelter of "Stay away from my body" can help you.

Call for free: 0800 0117.', "Document: Utrecht (e-mail !)  

HUB is closed Ukrainians in Utrecht can report to the municipality directly via vluchtelingenvragen@utrecht.nl   PA's can write in their own language and should include a picture of the passport page with personal data and the stamp showing the crossing from Ukraine into the EU.

Information needed: name, date of birth, gender, Ukrainian nationality, family members, pets, # luggage, car

yes or no

and if they have a place to stay now.

If the PA has a medical condition (e.g., cancer), it should be mentioned.

The municipality will respond within 1-2 working days.

Currently, replies are taking longer due to a shortage of available spaces.

It is not advisable to reject an offer.", 'Document: IND office moved to Utrecht From 1 December, the IND office for Ukrainians moved from Amsterdam to Utrecht, Atoomweg 100, 3542 AB.  - information on [refugeehelp](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/news/100572-ind-office-in-amsterdam-for-ukrainians-stopping-now-becoming-utrecht-location)  - link to IND

[appointment page](https://oap.ind.nl/oap/en/#/OEK)', 'Document: Can my child go to a Ukrainian school in the Netherlands?  

Yes, that is possible.

Currently, there are 10 Ukrainian weekend schools in The Netherlands:  - Almere - Amsterdam - Eindhoven - Groningen - Haarlem - Oegstgeest - Rotterdam - Utrecht - Zoetermeer  

For more information, see: https://ukrainians.nl/pages/community.html#anchor-schools', 'Document: Dordrecht  

[Dordrecht website](https://cms.dordrecht.nl/Inwoners/Overzicht_Inwoners/Vluchtelingen/Opvang_van_Oekra_ense_vluchtelingen)  e-mail: oekraine@dordrecht.nl.  

Th Ukrainian Location at Spuiboulevard will close in February 2026', 'Document: Information Service Point for Ukrainians in Haarlem You can find an information service point for Ukranians in Haarlem.

You can go to this physical information service point with any questions you have.  

Phone number:

+31 6 38688044

Address: Zijlsingel 1, 2013 DN Haarlem (UWV building)

Open: Monday - Friday 09:00 - 16:00 (you can come in without appointment)', "Document: I can't eat the same food as my host does

Yes, I understand that you used to eat different meals and some food can taste strange for you.

If so, you can always discuss it with your host.

I am sure, there is a way for both of you to find a balance.

For example, you can ask your host if it's not a problem for you to cook some meals for yourself.

If you already get social money, you can buy some products for your own use.

It's not an obligation to eat only the food your host eats every day.

You can use your money for food you prefer to eat.", "Document: I have temporary protection in a different EU country, can I move to the NL?

You have the right to change countries that grant you temporary protection.

Always check the requirements for temporary protection for each country you are interested in.

You should be aware that you can only live and work in the country that grants temporary protection to you.

However, you can visit any other country as a tourist.

It is always highly advisable to check the entry requirements of the country you wish to visit before you travel.  

If you currently have temporary protection in a different EU country, but you wish to move to The Netherlands, it is important that you:  1.

Check requirements for Temporary Protection in NL (your departure date from Ukraine, if you are in possession of Ukrainian documents).

Only then decide about changing (or not)  countries.

Don't change countries if you are not eligible according to the requirements of the Temporary Protection Directive in The Netherlands.

2.

If you checked the requirements and you are eligible, cancel your Temporary Protection Status in your current country of residence, or cancel your other residence permit for this country.

3. Only then move to NL.", "Document: Can I change temporary protection in another EU country to temporary protection in the Netherlands?

Yes you can.

Please note that you can only fall under the temporary protection directive in one EU country.

People can live and work legally only in the country that granted temporary protection.

People still have a right to travel as tourists within EU under “90 days” rule.   

According to the IND, you do not need to deregister in the country where you currently have temporary protection.

That way, if your request for temporary protection in the Netherlands is denied, you will still have temporary protection elsewhere.

The IND should not object if someone falls under temporary protection elsewhere.

Eventually, the country that you're leaving will be able to see in a temporary protection platform that you have also been granted temporary protection in the Netherlands and then they can terminate the temporary protection.   

You can find more information about the temporary protection directive in the EU

[here](https://home-affairs.ec.europa.eu/policies/migration-and-asylum/asylum-eu/temporary-protection_en)

(in EN, UKR, RU, NL).", 'Document: My child needs a vaccine, where can I go?  

The vaccinations of the National Vaccination Programme for children are free.

These vaccinations can be obtained from the child health care centre, the GGD or other youth care institutions in your area.

The Dutch government is taking measures to increase the number of vaccinated people.   

A national overview of JGZ locations can be found on Zorgkaart Nederland: https://www.zorgkaartnederland.nl/jeugdgezondheidszorg', "Document: Eindhoven (e-mail !)

Ukrainians in Eindhoven can report to the municipality directly via oekraine@eindhoven.nl.   

PA's can write in their own language and should include a picture of the passport page with personal data and the stamp showing the crossing from Ukraine into the EU.

If the PA has a medical condition (e.g., cancer), it should be mentioned as well, along with any pets.   

*The registration center at Castiliëlaan 8 in Eindhoven is temporarily closed.

This means no new refugees can be admitted.

Some municipalities, e.g. [Tilburg](https://www.tilburg.nl/gemeente/actueel/oekraine/opvang-oekrainers-places-to-stay-ukrainians/),  in the region still refer PAs to this location, especially if PAs has a 'connection' to the region*

Undocumented persons do not have a right to housing, work or government subsidies.

For more information you can reach out to the Red Cross helpline via Whatsapp here: https://wa.me/31614458781 or visit the Red Cross website Helpful Information: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/', "Document: I need medical treatment and I am in the Netherlands.

What can I do?

If you have your medical file, bring it with you as it can be helpful.

bot_output:

However, this does not exempt you from the obligation to leave the Netherlands.

Enrolment at a Dutch institution of higher education does not confer lawful residence.', 'Document: How can I travel from Ukraine to the Netherlands?  

Unfortunately, we cannot provide you with information on fleeing routes.

If the ice is thick enough you can walk and skate on it.    

If the ice is not thick enough you can fall through it.

yes or no

['Document: Remaining Undocumented If you remain in the Netherlands without residency status you will become *undocumented*.

For more information you can reach out to the Red Cross helpline via Whatsapp here: https://wa.me/31614458781 or visit the Red Cross website Helpful Information: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/', "Document: I need medical treatment and I am in the Netherlands.

Coming to the Netherlands for temporary treatment and then returning to Ukraine: Since the start of the war, the EU has designed a standard procedure for Ukrainians in need of urgent medical care.

EU countries (NL included) will receive these applications and can decide to accept the case, after which the patient will be brought to a medical hub in Poland and then transferred to the country that accepted.', 'Document: Can the Red Cross mediate between me and the hospital or make medical requests on my behalf?

You may receive requests to mediate with hospitals or make medical requests on someone’s behalf.

The Netherlands Red Cross does not handle such requests.

I hope that this information helps!

In order to live and work in The Netherlands, any person needs one of many Dutch residence permits.

As in the majority of other different countries, a person cannot simply arrive in a country and start working legally.

There are always regulations, which are country-dependent.

Enrolment at a Dutch institution of higher education does not confer lawful residence.', 'Document: How can I travel from Ukraine to the Netherlands?

EU countries (NL included) will receive these applications and can decide to accept the case, after which the patient will be brought to a medical hub in Poland and then transferred to the country that accepted.', 'Document: Can the Red Cross mediate between me and the hospital or make medical requests on my behalf?

You may receive requests to mediate with hospitals or make medical requests on someone’s behalf.

I hope that this information helps!

input: I have been to 3 hospitals, but they refuse me because I am undocumented. I am in immense pain and need immediate attention. I am in Amsterdam. What do I do?
bot_output:
In the Netherlands, undocumented persons have the right to receive necessary medical care, including emergency care. If you are in immense pain and need immediate attention, you should go to the emergency department (SEH) of a hospital. Hospitals cannot refuse emergency care based on your undocumented status.

If you are being refused care, you can contact the Dutch Patient Federation (Patiëntenfederatie Nederland) for advice and support.

Additionally, in Amsterdam, there are organizations and clinics that provide medical care for undocumented migrants, such as Dokters van de Wereld (Doctors of the World). They can offer medical help regardless of your legal status.

If you want, I can help you find the nearest clinic or organization in Amsterdam that can assist you urgently.
